seo.title: Security Checklist for Solana Developers
seo.description: A comprehensive checklist covering account validation, PDA security, CPI safety, and Solana program security best practices.

content.intro: Solana's account model creates unique security considerations. Use this checklist to ensure your programs are secure against common attack vectors.

items.text: Verify account owner matches expected program ID
Check account discriminator to ensure correct account type
Validate signer status for accounts that should authorize actions
Check writable flag for accounts that will be modified
Verify account is initialized before reading data
Validate account data length matches expected size
Check that accounts are not closed (lamports = 0)
Verify rent-exempt status for accounts that should persist
Use consistent seeds for PDA derivation across program and client
Store bump seed in account data to avoid recalculation
Validate PDA derivation on-chain, don't trust client-provided PDAs
Use create_program_address for validation, not find_program_address
Include unique identifiers in seeds to prevent collisions
Document seed structure clearly for maintainability
Use canonical bump (the one from find_program_address)
Keep total seed length under 32 bytes
Verify token account mint matches expected token
Check token account owner is the expected user/PDA
Validate token program ID (SPL Token vs Token-2022)
Account for token decimals in all calculations
Check token account is not frozen before transfers
Verify associated token account derivation
Handle close authority properly for token accounts
Check delegate and delegated amount for token accounts
Use checked arithmetic (checked_add, checked_sub, checked_mul)
Handle division by zero explicitly
Consider precision loss in division operations
Round in protocol's favor, not user's favor
Use saturating arithmetic where appropriate
Validate numeric inputs are within expected ranges
Use fixed-point math for financial calculations
Test edge cases with minimum and maximum values
Validate target program ID before CPI
Use hardcoded program IDs, not account-provided ones
Pass correct signer seeds for PDA-signed CPIs
Follow checks-effects-interactions pattern
Update state before making CPIs to prevent reentrancy
Check CPI return values for success
Limit CPIs to known, audited programs
Document CPI trust assumptions
Implement proper authority checks for admin functions
Use multi-sig or governance for critical operations
Implement upgrade authority controls
Add timelock for sensitive parameter changes
Document all privileged operations
Allow authority transfer/revocation
Validate authority accounts are signers
Consider program freezing for emergencies
Initialize all account fields explicitly
Use proper serialization/deserialization
Handle account resizing carefully
Clean up closed accounts properly
Prevent duplicate initialization
Use version field for future migrations
Validate state transitions are valid
Document account lifecycle
Use Clock sysvar for timestamps, not block data
Handle i64 timestamps correctly (not u64)
Consider slot vs Unix timestamp based on precision needs
Account for clock skew in time-sensitive operations
Don't trust future timestamps from users
Implement reasonable timelock durations
Write comprehensive unit tests with Bankrun
Test on devnet with realistic conditions
Test all error paths, not just happy paths
Use fuzzing (Trident) for complex logic
Test with invalid account inputs
Test arithmetic edge cases
Test CPI failure scenarios
Verify compute unit usage under load
Verify program builds are reproducible
Use verified builds on-chain
Store upgrade authority securely (multi-sig)
Test upgrade procedure before mainnet
Document deployment and upgrade process
Consider making program immutable after stabilization
Monitor program after deployment
Have incident response plan ready
